title: fix(spec): rewrite ConditionalValidationSchema TSDoc examples in evaluable CEL (#20026)
body:
Fixes #20026

Clause-②: no

## What changed

Every example predicate in the `ConditionalValidationSchema` TSDoc docblock (`packages/spec/src/data/validation.zod.ts`, ~lines 362-537) is rewritten in the CEL the evaluator actually accepts:

- 17 of 19 used `=` for comparison, or `AND`/`NOT`/`REGEX(...)` word-form operators — `@marcbachmann/cel-js` parses `=` as the start of an assignment (not equality) and CEL has no `AND`/`OR`/`NOT` keyword form, so every one was a parse error.
- 2 (`order_total > 10000`, `approval_amount > 50000`) named a bare field with no `record.` root — an unknown-variable type error.
- `REGEX(tax_id, "…")` is rewritten to the evaluator's registered stdlib function `matches(record.tax_id, "…")` — the CEL form it accepts, per `packages/formula/src/stdlib.ts:361` (`registerFunction('matches(dyn, dyn): bool', …)`), not a literal transliteration of the Salesforce-style name.
- The **Salesforce Approach** half of the "Salesforce Pattern Comparison" block (`IF(ISPICKVAL(...), AND(...), FALSE)`) is deliberately **untouched** — it documents Salesforce's own formula syntax, not CEL. Only the **ObjectStack Approach** half beneath it was rewritten.

`packages/spec/src/data/validation.test.ts`'s `ConditionalValidationSchema` fixtures that copy these strings verbatim move with them (parse-only — `ValidationRuleSchema.parse(...).not.toThrow()`, no CEL evaluation, so no behaviour changes): the six exact copies of Use Cases 1-3's original seven strings, plus `validation.test.ts`'s `order_value_validation` test's `condition: 'manager_approval = null'` → `'record.manager_approval == null'` — its `then` block's message ("Orders over $10,000 require manager approval") and its `otherwise` block are verbatim/structurally identical to Use Case 3, so it illustrates the same manager-approval use case one field-name spelling apart (`manager_approval` vs. the TSDoc's `manager_approval_id`) and moves with it.

No schema, behaviour, or public export changes — TSDoc text only, in the same two files the strings already lived in, plus the changeset.

## Evaluation transcript (`ExpressionEngine.evaluate`, `@objectstack/formula`)

Every rewritten predicate evaluated once against a record that makes it `true` and one that makes it `false` (plus one extra disjunct check on the Use Case 5 regex branch):

| where | rewritten CEL | true-record | true result | false-record | false result |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| Use Case 1: when | `record.account_type == 'enterprise'` | `{"account_type":"enterprise"}` | `{"ok":true,"value":true}` OK | `{"account_type":"smb"}` | `{"ok":true,"value":false}` OK |
| Use Case 1: condition | `record.approval_status == null` | `{"approval_status":null}` | `{"ok":true,"value":true}` OK | `{"approval_status":"approved"}` | `{"ok":true,"value":false}` OK |
| Use Case 2: when | `record.requires_shipping == true` | `{"requires_shipping":true}` | `{"ok":true,"value":true}` OK | `{"requires_shipping":false}` | `{"ok":true,"value":false}` OK |
| Use Case 2: condition | `record.shipping_address == null \|\| record.shipping_address == ''` | `{"shipping_address":null}` | `{"ok":true,"value":true}` OK | `{"shipping_address":"123 Main St"}` | `{"ok":true,"value":false}` OK |
| Use Case 3: when | `record.order_total > 10000` | `{"order_total":15000}` | `{"ok":true,"value":true}` OK | `{"order_total":5000}` | `{"ok":true,"value":false}` OK |
| Use Case 3: then.condition | `record.manager_approval_id == null` | `{"manager_approval_id":null}` | `{"ok":true,"value":true}` OK | `{"manager_approval_id":"user_123"}` | `{"ok":true,"value":false}` OK |
| Use Case 3: otherwise.condition | `record.payment_method == null` | `{"payment_method":null}` | `{"ok":true,"value":true}` OK | `{"payment_method":"credit_card"}` | `{"ok":true,"value":false}` OK |
| Use Case 4: when | `record.region == 'EU'` | `{"region":"EU"}` | `{"ok":true,"value":true}` OK | `{"region":"US"}` | `{"ok":true,"value":false}` OK |
| Use Case 4: then.condition | `record.gdpr_consent_given == false` | `{"gdpr_consent_given":false}` | `{"ok":true,"value":true}` OK | `{"gdpr_consent_given":true}` | `{"ok":true,"value":false}` OK |
| Use Case 4: otherwise.condition | `record.tos_accepted == false` | `{"tos_accepted":false}` | `{"ok":true,"value":true}` OK | `{"tos_accepted":true}` | `{"ok":true,"value":false}` OK |
| Use Case 5: when (outer) | `record.country == 'US'` | `{"country":"US"}` | `{"ok":true,"value":true}` OK | `{"country":"CA"}` | `{"ok":true,"value":false}` OK |
| Use Case 5: when (nested) | `record.state == 'CA'` | `{"state":"CA"}` | `{"ok":true,"value":true}` OK | `{"state":"NY"}` | `{"ok":true,"value":false}` OK |
| Use Case 5: nested condition (matches/regex) | `record.tax_id == null \|\| !matches(record.tax_id, "^\d{2}-\d{7}$")` | `{"tax_id":null}` | `{"ok":true,"value":true}` OK | `{"tax_id":"12-3456789"}` | `{"ok":true,"value":false}` OK |
| Use Case 5: nested condition (wrong-shape tax_id, extra check) | same | `{"tax_id":"not-a-tax-id"}` | `{"ok":true,"value":true}` OK | n/a | n/a |
| Use Case 6: when | `record.is_taxable == true` | `{"is_taxable":true}` | `{"ok":true,"value":true}` OK | `{"is_taxable":false}` | `{"ok":true,"value":false}` OK |
| Use Case 6: condition | `record.tax_code == null \|\| record.tax_code == ''` | `{"tax_code":null}` | `{"ok":true,"value":true}` OK | `{"tax_code":"VAT-1"}` | `{"ok":true,"value":false}` OK |
| Use Case 7: when | `record.user_role == 'manager'` | `{"user_role":"manager"}` | `{"ok":true,"value":true}` OK | `{"user_role":"rep"}` | `{"ok":true,"value":false}` OK |
| Use Case 7: condition | `record.approval_amount > 50000` | `{"approval_amount":75000}` | `{"ok":true,"value":true}` OK | `{"approval_amount":10000}` | `{"ok":true,"value":false}` OK |
| Salesforce comparison: when | `record.type == 'enterprise'` | `{"type":"enterprise"}` | `{"ok":true,"value":true}` OK | `{"type":"smb"}` | `{"ok":true,"value":false}` OK |
| Salesforce comparison: then.condition | `record.amount > 100000 && record.approval == null` | `{"amount":150000,"approval":null}` | `{"ok":true,"value":true}` OK | `{"amount":150000,"approval":"user_1"}` | `{"ok":true,"value":false}` OK |

**ALL 20 checks: true-branch and false-branch (or the extra disjunct) evaluate as expected.**

Lit control — every ORIGINAL (pre-fix) string, same evaluator: all 19 still fail (`parse: Unexpected character: =` ×16, `type: Unknown variable` ×2, `parse: Unexpected character: 'D'` on the `AND` keyword ×1). None evaluate.

## dist confirmation (H2)

Before this fix (measured on `origin/main` `4df101c383` via `packages/spec/dist/object.zod-*.d.ts` built from unmodified source): every one of the seven originally-graded broken strings (e.g. `account_type = "enterprise"`, `order_total > 10000`) is present verbatim in the published `.d.ts` — confirms the card's "ships in the published spec d.ts" claim.

After this fix, rebuilt `@objectstack/spec`: `grep -c` on `packages/spec/dist/object.zod-*.d.ts` for each of the 19 new strings returns exactly 1; `grep -c` for every one of the 19 original broken strings (properly anchored, not as a loose substring of the new ones) returns 0.

## Local verification

- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec build && pnpm --filter @objectstack/formula build` — both build clean.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec check:generated` — 15/15 generated artifacts up to date (check:docs, check:api-surface, check:authorable-surface, etc.) — no drift from the TSDoc edit.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec exec vitest run src/data/validation.test.ts` — 72/72 tests pass.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec run typecheck` — clean (`tsc --noEmit`, `check:scripts-typecheck`, `check:test-typecheck` all OK; the 255 pre-existing debt errors are the shrink-only ledger, untouched by this diff).
- `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack --ran ran.list`: **82 derived families, 79 run (all green), 3 NOT-MEASURED** (`check:dual-build-cjs-loads`, `check:lean-entry-closure`, `check:type-check-debt` — each refuses its own prerequisite, `PREREQUISITE NOT MET` exit 3, because they need the FULL workspace build closure per `check-type-check-coverage.mjs`'s own prescription — out of this card's local scope, left to CI's Build Core lane). 0 unrun.
- Read `packages/lint/scripts/check-doc-formula-expressions.mjs` (the #6763 gate) directly and then ran it (`pnpm --filter @objectstack/lint run check:doc-formula-expressions`, exit 0): its spec-TSDoc surface only scans `@example`-tagged JSDoc bodies via a registered slot allowlist (`SPEC_EXAMPLE_SLOTS`); our block is an untagged prose docblock (`## Use Cases`), so this gate never touched it, before or after — consistent with "⛔ no new gate: #6763 closed that question."

## Acceptance notes

- `content/docs/protocol/objectql/index.mdx:186` (`condition: "account_type = 'Enterprise' AND contract_value = null"`) carries the same non-CEL spelling in an unrelated docs page; already recorded, unresolved, in `docs/audits/2026-06-handwritten-docs-accuracy-followups.md`. Left untouched — out of this card's scope and no additionally measured reach beyond what that audit already recorded.
- `validation.test.ts`'s nested-conditional test (`should accept nested conditional validation`, ~lines 549-570) also uses `when: 'country = "US"'` / nested `when: 'state = "CA"'` / `condition: 'tax_id = null'`, coincidentally matching the now-fixed Use Case 5 strings — but it is a separate, independently-named parse-only fixture, not a verbatim copy of a Use Case 5 string keyed to the same test name/message text the way the seven (now eight) moved fixtures are. Left unchanged.
